```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse   = TRUE,
  comment    = "#>",
  fig.width  = 7,
  fig.height = 3.2,
  dev        = "png",
  dpi        = 192
)
set.seed(42)
```

```{css echo = FALSE}
img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
```

SeqPlotR attaches legend metadata to the elements that draw the data. A `LegendKey` describes one glyph-plus-label row and a `SeqLegendSpec` (from `seq_legend()`) says where to lay rows out. For continuous scales, `seq_gradient_legend()` produces a color bar. Legends are also generated automatically when `map()` binds `color`, `fill` or `shape` to a column. Three positions are supported:

| Position | Where it renders |
|----------|-----------------|
| `"inside"` | Overlaid on the data panel. |
| `"track_margin"` | In the canvas margin beside one track. |
| `"canvas_margin"` | Aggregated from all tracks into one margin band. |

## Data

```{r load}
library(SeqPlotR)
library(GenomicRanges)

win <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(1, 1e6))

# sparse ChIP-like signal with sharp peaks
make_chip <- function(n = 200, n_peaks = 8, seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  starts <- sort(sample(1:999000, n))
  scores <- runif(n, 0, 0.15)
  for (pk in sort(sample(seq_len(n), n_peaks))) {
    w <- max(1, pk - 3):min(n, pk + 3)
    scores[w] <- scores[w] + runif(length(w), 0.4, 0.85)
  }
  GRanges("chr1", IRanges(starts, width = 1), score = pmin(scores, 1))
}
gr_a <- make_chip(seed = 1)
gr_b <- make_chip(seed = 2)

# continuous scores for gradient examples
set.seed(42)
gr_cnt <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(sort(sample(1:999000, 120)), width = 1),
                  score = round(runif(120, 0, 100), 1))

# contact-map-like tiles
n_bins <- 60
starts_hic <- seq(1, 1e6, length.out = n_bins + 1)[-(n_bins + 1)]
pairs <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(n_bins), j = seq_len(n_bins))
pairs <- pairs[pairs$j >= pairs$i, ]
gr_tiles <- GRanges("chr1", IRanges(starts_hic[pairs$i], width = 1e6 / n_bins),
                    y = pairs$j,
                    fill = pmax(0, pmin(1, round(exp(-(pairs$j - pairs$i) * 0.08) +
                                                   rnorm(nrow(pairs), 0, 0.05), 3))))

# simulated chromothripsis on chr3: somatic SNVs and copy-number segments
sim <- function(f) utils::read.delim(system.file("extdata", "sim", "ct", f, package = "SeqPlotR"))
snv <- sim("snvs.tsv")
snv <- GRanges(snv$chrom, IRanges(snv$pos, width = 1), vaf = snv$vaf, depth = snv$depth,
               sbs6 = snv$sbs6, clonality = ifelse(snv$clonal, "clonal", "subclonal"))
seg <- sim("segments.tsv")
seg <- GRanges(seg$chrom, IRanges(seg$start, seg$end), cn = seg$cn,
               state = ifelse(seg$cn > 2, "gain", ifelse(seg$cn < 2, "loss", "neutral")))
win_ct <- GRanges("chr3", IRanges(9.5e7, 1.95e8))

# right margin wide enough for auto-generated legends
right_margin <- aes(margins = list(top = 0, right = 0.25, bottom = 0, left = 0))
```

# Manual legends

## Inside

A bare `LegendKey` passed to `legend` is auto-placed at the panel centre.

```{r inside-bare, fig.cap = "A bare LegendKey is auto-placed at the panel centre."}
p1 <- seq_plot() %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(
    aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8),
    legend     = LegendKey(label = "H3K27ac",
                           color = "#A02020", fill = "#D08080", shape = "-")
  )
p1$plot()
```

`seq_legend()` pins the legend to a corner. `x` and `y` are fractions of the panel; `hjust = 1` right-aligns the block and `orientation = "horizontal"` puts the keys in one row.

```{r inside-anchored, fig.cap = "seq_legend() anchors the legend to the top-left corner with a title."}
k1 <- LegendKey(label = "H3K27ac", color = "#A02020", fill = "#D08080", shape = "-")
k2 <- LegendKey(label = "H3K4me3", color = "#205080", fill = "#8090C0", shape = "-")

spec_inside <- seq_legend(
  list(k1, k2),
  title       = "ChIP marks",
  position    = "inside",
  x           = 0.02,   # 2% from the left edge
  y           = 0.95,   # 95% of the way up the panel
  orientation = "vertical"
)

p2 <- seq_plot() %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(
    aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8),
    legend     = spec_inside
  )
p2$plot()
```

```{r inside-horizontal, fig.cap = "Two keys in a horizontal row, right-aligned at the top."}
spec_h <- seq_legend(
  list(k1, k2),
  title       = "ChIP marks",
  position    = "inside",
  x           = 0.98, hjust = 1,   # right-align
  y           = 0.95,
  orientation = "horizontal"
)

p3 <- seq_plot() %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(
    aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8),
    legend     = spec_h
  )
p3$plot()
```

## Track margin

`"track_margin"` draws the legend in the margin beside one track. Set `side` and enlarge the matching plot margin to make room.

```{r track-margin, fig.cap = "Two-key vertical legend in the 18% left canvas margin beside the track."}
spec_tm <- seq_legend(
  list(k1, k2),
  title       = "ChIP marks",
  position    = "track_margin",
  side        = "left",
  orientation = "vertical",
  x           = 0.1,    # fraction of margin width
  y           = 0.8     # fraction of margin height (0 = bottom, 1 = top)
)

p_tm <- seq_plot(
  aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top   = 0.03, bottom = 0.03,
                                   left  = 0.18, right  = 0.03))
) %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(
    aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8),
    legend     = spec_tm
  )
p_tm$plot()
```

`orientation` defaults to `"vertical"` for left and right sides and `"horizontal"` for top and bottom:

```{r margin-orientation}
seq_legend(k1, position = "track_margin", side = "left")$orientation
seq_legend(k1, position = "track_margin", side = "top")$orientation
```

## Canvas margin

`"canvas_margin"` collects entries from all tracks and renders them once across the chosen margin. Specs sharing a `title` merge under one heading; differing titles are separated into groups. Use `%__%` to stack the tracks.

```{r canvas-margin, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Two stacked tracks sharing a single canvas-margin legend at the top."}
# Each spec carries the key for one track.
# The first spec's x / hjust controls alignment of the aggregated block.
spec_ca <- seq_legend(k1, title = "ChIP marks", position = "canvas_margin",
                      side = "top", x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)
spec_cb <- seq_legend(k2, title = "ChIP marks", position = "canvas_margin",
                      side = "top")

p_cm <- seq_plot(
  aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top   = 0.12, bottom = 0.04,
                                   left  = 0.04, right  = 0.04))
) %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8), legend = spec_ca) %__%
  seq_track(data = gr_b, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#8090C0", alpha = 0.8), legend = spec_cb)

p_cm$plot()
```

```{r canvas-margin-groups, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Two title groups separated in the canvas margin."}
spec_ca2 <- seq_legend(k1, title = "Active enhancers",
                       position = "canvas_margin", side = "top",
                       x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)
spec_cb2 <- seq_legend(k2, title = "Promoters",
                       position = "canvas_margin", side = "top")

p_cm2 <- seq_plot(
  aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top   = 0.14, bottom = 0.04,
                                   left  = 0.04, right  = 0.04))
) %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8), legend = spec_ca2) %__%
  seq_track(data = gr_b, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(aesthetics = aes(fill = "#8090C0", alpha = 0.8), legend = spec_cb2)

p_cm2$plot()
```

# Gradient color bars

`seq_gradient_legend()` renders a filled bar graded from the palette's low to high colour with a tick axis. Placement arguments (`position`, `x`, `y`, `hjust`, `orientation`, `side`) work as in `seq_legend()`.

## Manual placement

```{r gradient-inside, fig.cap = "Vertical viridis color bar pinned to the right side of the panel."}
grad_inside <- seq_gradient_legend(
  palette     = "viridis",
  limits      = c(0, 100),
  title       = "Score",
  position    = "inside",
  x           = 0.97,          # near the right edge
  y           = 0.5,           # vertically centred
  hjust       = 1,
  orientation = "vertical"
)

p_gi <- seq_plot() %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_cnt, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_point(
    aesthetics = aes(color = "#2166AC", size = 1.2),
    legend     = grad_inside
  )
p_gi$plot()
```

Place the bar in the track margin for a clean separation from the data:

```{r gradient-track-margin, fig.cap = "Horizontal plasma color bar in the right track margin."}
grad_tm <- seq_gradient_legend(
  palette     = "plasma",
  limits      = c(0, 100),
  title       = "Score",
  position    = "track_margin",
  side        = "right",
  orientation = "vertical",
  x           = 0.5,
  y           = 0.5
)

p_gtm <- seq_plot(
  aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top    = 0.03, bottom = 0.03,
                                   left   = 0.03, right  = 0.20))
) %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_cnt, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_point(
    aesthetics = aes(color = "#2166AC", size = 1.2),
    legend     = grad_tm
  )
p_gtm$plot()
```

## Tick breaks

`breaks` is `NULL` (default `pretty()` ticks), a single integer (`pretty()` targeting that many ticks), or a numeric vector of exact values.

```{r gradient-breaks, fig.cap = "Color bar with explicit breaks at 0, 25, 50, 75, 100."}
grad_breaks <- seq_gradient_legend(
  palette     = "magma",
  limits      = c(0, 100),
  breaks      = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100),
  title       = "Score",
  position    = "inside",
  x           = 0.97,
  y           = 0.5,
  hjust       = 1,
  orientation = "vertical"
)

p_brk <- seq_plot() %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_cnt, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_point(
    aesthetics = aes(color = "#8B3A8B", size = 1.2),
    legend     = grad_breaks
  )
p_brk$plot()
```

A gradient legend attached to a `seq_tile` heatmap:

```{r heatmap-labelled, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = "Contact-map heatmap with a four-tick gradient legend placed inside."}
hleg <- seq_gradient_legend(
  palette     = "reds",
  limits      = c(0, 1),
  title       = "Contact\nfrequency",
  breaks      = 4,
  x           = 0.72, y = 0.95,
  orientation = "vertical",
  position    = "inside"
)

p11 <- seq_plot(
  aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top = 0.04, bottom = 0.04,
                                   left = 0.04, right = 0.04))
) %+%
  seq_track(windows = win) %+%
  seq_tile(
    data    = gr_tiles,
    mapping = map(x = start, y = y, fill = fill),
    legend  = hleg
  )
p11$plot()
```

# Automatic legends

Mapping a column to `color`, `fill` or `shape` generates a legend with no `seq_legend()` call. Discrete columns give a keyed legend (flexoki palette; shapes cycle circle, square, triangle, diamond) and numeric columns give a viridis color bar. Auto-legends go in the right track margin, so reserve space with the plot-level `margins` aesthetic. An explicit `legend` always overrides auto-generation.

The examples below use a simulated chromothripsis sample. `snv` holds its somatic SNVs on chr3 (variant allele fraction, read depth, the six-class mutation type `sbs6`, and whether the SNV is clonal), and `seg` holds its copy-number segments, where the shattered region between 100 and 190 Mb oscillates between copy number 3 and 1.

Mapping `color` to the mutation type gives a six-level discrete legend:

```{r auto-discrete, fig.cap = "Six-level discrete color legend for SNV mutation type in the right track margin."}
p1 <- seq_plot(aesthetics = right_margin) %+%
  seq_track(data = snv, mapping = map(x = start, y = vaf), windows = win_ct) %+%
  seq_point(
    aesthetics = aes(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.7),
    mapping    = map(color = sbs6)
  )
p1$plot()
```

Mapping `shape` to clonality marks clonal and subclonal SNVs with different glyphs:

```{r auto-shape, fig.cap = "Shape legend auto-generated from map(shape = clonality) in the right track margin."}
p2 <- seq_plot(aesthetics = right_margin) %+%
  seq_track(data = snv, mapping = map(x = start, y = vaf), windows = win_ct) %+%
  seq_point(
    aesthetics = aes(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.7),
    mapping    = map(shape = clonality)
  )
p2$plot()
```

A numeric column gives a color bar. Here read depth is on the y axis, which drops where the copy number falls to 1, and the color shows the variant allele fraction:

```{r auto-continuous, fig.cap = "Viridis color bar with auto tick axis for SNV variant allele fraction."}
p3 <- seq_plot(aesthetics = right_margin) %+%
  seq_track(data = snv, mapping = map(x = start, y = depth), windows = win_ct) %+%
  seq_point(
    aesthetics = aes(size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8),
    mapping    = map(color = vaf)
  )
p3$plot()
```

The same applies to other elements, including `seq_bar`, `seq_segment` and `seq_tile` heatmaps. Copy-number segments drawn as bars take their fill from the gain, loss or neutral state:

```{r auto-bar-discrete, fig.cap = "Copy-number segment bars with a discrete fill legend from map(fill = state)."}
p4 <- seq_plot(aesthetics = right_margin) %+%
  seq_track(data = seg, mapping = map(x = start, y = cn), windows = win_ct,
            scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 3.2))) %+%
  seq_bar(
    aesthetics = aes(alpha = 0.85),
    mapping    = map(x = start, y = cn, fill = state)
  )
p4$plot()
```

`seq_segment` draws one horizontal line per copy-number segment, colored by state:

```{r auto-segment, fig.cap = "seq_segment with a discrete color legend from map(color = state)."}
p5 <- seq_plot(aesthetics = right_margin) %+%
  seq_track(data = seg, mapping = map(x = start, y = cn), windows = win_ct,
            scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 3.5))) %+%
  seq_segment(
    aesthetics = aes(linewidth = 3),
    mapping    = map(x = start, x_end = end, y = cn, y_end = cn, color = state)
  )
p5$plot()
```

A numeric fill gives a gradient. Here the bar fill follows the integer copy number:

```{r auto-gradient-bar, fig.cap = "Copy-number segment bars with a continuous fill gradient from map(fill = cn)."}
p6 <- seq_plot(aesthetics = right_margin) %+%
  seq_track(data = seg, mapping = map(x = start, y = cn), windows = win_ct,
            scale_y = seq_scale_continuous(limits = c(0, 3.2))) %+%
  seq_bar(
    mapping = map(x = start, y = cn, fill = cn)
  )
p6$plot()
```

The tile heatmap keeps the contact-map tiles, since the simulated data has no contact matrix:

```{r auto-heatmap, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = "Contact-map tiles with auto gradient legend."}
p7 <- seq_plot(
  aesthetics = aes(margins = list(top = 0.04, bottom = 0.04,
                                   left = 0.04, right = 0.25))
) %+%
  seq_track(windows = win) %+%
  seq_tile(
    data    = gr_tiles,
    mapping = map(x = start, y = y, fill = fill)
  )
p7$plot()
```

# Suppression

Each level overrides the finer levels below it. `show_legend = FALSE` on an element silences only that element, including its auto-generated bar or legend:

```{r suppress-element}
el_shown  <- seq_area(legend = LegendKey(label = "Foreground"))
el_hidden <- seq_area(legend = LegendKey(label = "Background"),
                      show_legend = FALSE)

is.null(el_shown$collect_legend_keys())   # FALSE — contributes
is.null(el_hidden$collect_legend_keys())  # TRUE  — suppressed
```

```{r suppress-element-auto}
el_no_bar <- seq_bar(mapping = map(fill = score), show_legend = FALSE)
is.null(el_no_bar$auto_legend)   # TRUE — no bar generated
```

On a track it silences every element in that track:

```{r suppress-track}
trk <- seq_track(windows = win,
                 elements  = list(el_shown, el_hidden),
                 show_legend = FALSE)
is.null(trk$collect_legend_keys())   # TRUE — whole track suppressed
```

`legend = FALSE` (or `show_legend = FALSE`) on `seq_plot()` removes all legend output, auto-generated included:

```{r suppress-plot, fig.cap = "legend = FALSE on seq_plot() removes all legend output."}
p_no_legend <- seq_plot(legend = FALSE) %+%
  seq_track(data = gr_a, mapping = map(x = start, y = score),
            windows = win) %+%
  seq_area(
    aesthetics = aes(fill = "#D08080", alpha = 0.8),
    legend     = spec_inside   # spec defined earlier — ignored here
  )
p_no_legend$plot()
```

# Inspecting legend metadata

`collect_legend_keys()` aggregates entries from an element, a track, or all tracks in a plot. It returns `NULL` when nothing contributes, otherwise a list with `title`, `key` and `element_class`.

```{r collect-element}
k  <- LegendKey(label = "ChIP signal", title = "Tracks", color = "darkgreen")
el <- seq_area(legend = k)
str(el$collect_legend_keys()[[1]])
```

```{r collect-track}
el1 <- seq_area(legend = LegendKey(label = "H3K27ac", color = "#A02020"))
el2 <- seq_area(legend = LegendKey(label = "H3K4me3", color = "#205080"))

trk  <- seq_track(windows = win, elements = list(el1, el2))
keys <- trk$collect_legend_keys()
cat(length(keys), "keys from track:\n")
for (entry in keys)
  cat(" ", entry$key$label, "—", entry$element_class, "\n")
```

# Summary

| Task | How |
|------|-----|
| Attach a legend, auto-placed at panel centre | `seq_area(legend = LegendKey(...))` |
| Anchor to a corner | `seq_legend(keys, position = "inside", x =, y =)` |
| Beside one track | `seq_legend(keys, position = "track_margin", side =)` plus a wider margin |
| One band for all tracks | `seq_legend(keys, position = "canvas_margin", side =)` |
| Continuous color bar | `seq_gradient_legend(palette =, limits =, breaks =)` |
| Automatic legend | `map(color = col)`, `map(fill = col)` or `map(shape = col)` |
| Suppress | `show_legend = FALSE` on an element or track; `legend = FALSE` on the plot |

| Palette | Colors |
|---------|--------|
| `"viridis"` | purple, teal, yellow (default) |
| `"plasma"` | dark blue, magenta, yellow |
| `"magma"` | black, red, cream |
| `"blues"` | white to navy |
| `"reds"` | white to dark red |
